name: elements
description: What every element asks of its helpers: tool tip, cursor, fluent symbol, automation name, resources, and the focus pair of UIElement.

ToolTip.comment: One text, two homes: ToolTipService's hover hint and AutomationProperties.Name, the name a screen reader speaks. Set together deliberately -- the property exists for controls whose face is a glyph rather than a word, and such a control needs naming in both places or it is nameless in one of them.

AutomationName.comment: The name a screen reader speaks, and nothing else -- the half of ToolTip that carries no hover hint. What needs it is the element whose face is already words but not text: a list row built out of a panel says nothing at all to automation, because a Button's accessible name comes from its content only when that content is a string. A hint on such a row would be noise, so the two are separate properties rather than one.

Cursor.comment: The pointer's shape over the element. WinUI keeps it on UIElement.ProtectedCursor, which the metadata marks protected -- but protected is a word for projections, not for the ABI: IUIElementProtected is an ordinary interface any element's object answers QueryInterface for, so the wrapper sets it on a plain Border with no subclass in between. The value is the metadata's own InputSystemCursorShape; a second vocabulary for Arrow, Hand and SizeWestEast would name nothing new.

Symbol.comment: The same property, spelled with the other enumeration. Symbol names 197 glyphs, chosen for Windows 8 and living in the E1xx compatibility block; FluentSymbol names all 1533 the documentation of Segoe Fluent Icons carries, E700 and up. Both are code points in the font SymbolIcon already draws with, so this is one property with two vocabularies rather than two ways of doing a thing -- and it is why an icon whose name Symbol never had (QuietHours, Brightness) needs no FontIcon and no font name. The metadata declares one setter; this is the second overload of it, and the generator keeps both because it deduplicates on the signature.
